metadata.description: Post-Rust OTP/2FA hashing migration performance comparison

otp_hashing.description: OTP hashing and verification - Rust SHA-256+salt vs bcrypt (cost 10)
components: server/napi-core/src/lib.rs (hash_otp, verify_otp_hash, constant_time_compare via sha2 + rand crates)
server/models/OTP.js (hashOTP, compareOTP updated to use native with fallback)

findings.hash_speedup: Rust SHA-256+salt is 10,414x faster than bcrypt (0.02ms vs 205ms)
findings.verify_speedup: Rust verification is 19,836x faster than bcrypt (0.01ms vs 207ms)
findings.security_sufficient: For 6-digit OTPs (1M possible values, 10-min TTL, single-use), SHA-256+salt provides adequate security versus bcrypt
findings.legacy_support: Rust verifyOtpHash detects bcrypt hashes ($2b$) and returns false, triggering JS bcrypt.compare fallback
findings.constant_time: constant_time_compare uses XOR-based constant-time algorithm to prevent timing side-channel attacks
findings.backup_codes: 2FA backup code verification updated from indexOf (timing-vulnerable) to constantTimeCompare (timing-safe)

conclusion: OTP/2FA hashing migrated to Rust. 10,000x+ speedup over bcrypt. Constant-time comparison prevents timing attacks. Legacy bcrypt hashes still supported via fallback.
